newsitem.title: USA: Palladium prices soar to 17-year high.
newsitem.headline: Palladium prices soar to 17-year high.

text.p: Palladium prices soared to 17-year highs Wednesday, and platinum prices ended higher, as a five-month suspension of Russian exports left the market acutely short of supplies.

"The Russians, the world's largest suppliers of palladium, are expected to resume supplies in late June, but in the meantime stockpiles have been run down and fabricators and dealers are trying to borrow the metal to cover their needs to avoid paying the high spot prices," said Ted Kempf, an analyst with CPM Group in New York.

Spot platinum in New York soared to about $233 an ounce, its highest level in at least 17 years. At the New York Mercantile Exchange, Palladium for delivery in June ended up $21.15 an ounce at $202.80.
Earlier in London palladium was priced at $210 an ounce, its highest level since 1989.

Prior to the start of trading in New York, Russian officials told Japanese traders Russian exports would resume on June 20, but they also said the export licenses had still not yet been granted by the Ministry of Foreign Economic Relations, suggesting further delays were likely, analysts said.

Russia supplies about 60 percent of the world's palladium and about 20 percent of its platinum. Both white metals are used in pollution control devices in the auto industry, in computer manufacturing and in platinum's case in jewelry.
Both metals have soared since the start of the year -- palladium is up 85 percent and platinum 25 percent -- due to administrative delays in Russian supplies to key importer Japan.
